header.title: Player guide
header.intro: Gachapon has two loops: you <collect>pull capsules</collect> to fill your collection, and you <battle>send your cards into battle</battle> in the campaign, the towers and team raids. This guide explains how it all works.

monnaies.intro: Six resources. Tokens, energy, dust and gold are shown in the top bar; unspent skill points show up as a badge on the Skills link.

i1.title: Tokens
i1.text: One token, one capsule. They refill on their own up to a cap.

i2.title: Dust
i2.text: Comes from recycling duplicates, quests, the login streak and level milestones. Spent in the daily shop, on wishes, energy packs and boosts, on levelling your cards, and on resetting the skill tree.

i3.title: Gold
i3.text: Earned in battles and raids. Spent on your cards' level, on upgrading equipment, and on token packs.

i4.title: Energy
i4.text: Your combat points. Every campaign or tower battle costs some; it refills on its own up to a cap.

i5.title: XP & level
i5.text: Earned by pulling and fighting. Your account goes up to level 100.

i6.title: Skill points
i6.text: One per level, plus bonuses at some milestones. You spend them in the skill tree.

tokens.intro: Every pull costs a token. They refill continuously, even while you're offline.

list.i1: Your stock has a cap. Tokens regenerated past it are lost, unless you have the Overflow skill, which turns them into dust.
list.i2: The top bar shows your balance and the time until the next token.

tokens.info: Other ways to get tokens: token packs in the shop (paid in gold), quests, the login streak, level milestones and the raid. Several skills and the Token flow team bonus speed up regeneration or raise the cap.
tokens.tip: Spend your tokens before you hit the cap, or invest in the cap early if you don't drop by often.

pulls.intro: A pull costs one token and gives you a random card from the active sets. Each card has a weight: the higher it is, the more often the card drops.

list.i1: You can pull one at a time, or ten at once with <pill>Pull x10</pill>.
list.i2: The result shows the card, its variant, and whether it's new to you.
list.i3: Your pity counter goes up with every pull (see below).

pulls.skills: Several skills affect pulls: they raise the odds of RARE EPIC LEGENDARY cards and of variants, give a chance of a free pull, or trigger a golden ball that forces a minimum rarity. Wish Granted can swap the card you pulled for one from your wishlist, of the same rarity.
pulls.info: The shop also sells boosts: for a few pulls, they raise the odds of the higher rarities.

rarete.intro: There are five rarities, from most to least common:
rarete.variantIntro: A RARE, EPIC or LEGENDARY card can drop as a variant:

list.i1: <pill>NORMAL</pill> the standard version, by far the most common.
list.i3: <pill>HOLOGRAPHIC</pill> the rarest of the three, with a rainbow sheen.

rarete.outro: The higher the rarity, the more often variants drop: a legendary is more likely to be holographic than a rare. Each variant counts as a separate card: pulling the brilliant version of a card you own in normal is not a duplicate.

piete.intro: Pity guarantees a legendary after a set number of pulls. A counter goes up with every pull that doesn't give one.

list.i1: When the counter reaches the threshold, your next pull is a legendary.
list.i2: Any legendary, from pity or not, resets the counter to zero.
list.i3: The counter is yours alone and carries over between sessions.

piete.info: Your counter is shown on the Play page and in the rate details. The Fate skill lowers the threshold.

doublon.intro: When you pull a card you already own, in the same variant, it's a duplicate: the copy goes on your stack, nothing is lost.

list.i1: Duplicates are used for ascension: moving a card up to the next tier costs one.
list.i2: You can also recycle a duplicate into dust from the collection. The amount depends on rarity.
list.i3: Recycle everything converts all your spare copies at once, up to the rarity you pick (normal variant only).

doublon.uses: Dust is spent in the daily shop, on wishes, on levelling your cards, on energy packs and boosts, and on resetting the skill tree.
doublon.tip: Keep duplicates of the cards you fight with: without them, no ascension. The Recycling skill increases the dust you get.

boutique.intro: The shop lets you target specific cards instead of leaving everything to chance, and sells resources.

i1.title: Daily shop
i1.text: A selection of cards that renews every day at midnight (UTC), bought with dust, priced by rarity. Skills add slots, lower prices and raise the rarities on offer.

i2.title: Wishes
i2.text: Set aside the cards you want and buy them with dust whenever you like, with no wait. It's full price: more expensive than the daily shop, no discounts, and always the normal variant. You start with 2 slots, up to 5 with the Collector skill.

i3.title: Packs & boosts
i3.text: Token packs cost gold. Energy packs cost dust, are limited per day, and can take your energy past its cap. Boosts, paid in dust, raise the odds of the higher rarities for a few pulls. There are cosmetics too.

niveaux.intro: Your account level goes up with the XP you earn by pulling and fighting, up to level 100.

list.i1: Every level gives a skill point. Levels 10, 25, 50, 75 and 100 also give bonus points and a bundle of tokens and dust.
list.i2: Every level-up refills your energy to the max.
list.i3: Skills raise the XP you get from pulling (Fervor) and fighting (Veteran).

niveaux.info: Don't mix up your account level (your progress) and a card's level (its combat power, see "Upgrading your cards").

competences.intro: You spend skill points in the tree; each node gives a permanent bonus. The full tree costs exactly what you earn up to level 100. It has four branches:

i1.title: Flux
i1.text: Your tokens: regeneration, cap, bonus tokens, free pulls, Overflow, and pull XP.

i2.title: Fortune
i2.text: Luck: rarity odds, golden ball, Wish Granted, pity threshold (Fate), variant rates (Prism) and the daily energy pack limit (Opulence).

i3.title: Collection
i3.text: Dust and the shop: recycling, discounts, the dust cost of card levels, gold prices, daily shop rarities and slots, wish slots.

i4.title: Combat
i4.text: Energy (cap and regeneration), gold earned, multiple battle cost, combat XP, drops, and equipment (upgrades and selling).

competences.info: You can reset the tree at any time for dust, based on how many points you've invested: every point comes back to you.

campagne.intro: The campaign has nine chapters (Plains, Whispering Forest, Ashes, Ocean, Crystals, Volcano, Tundra, Abyss, Rift), each with 10 stages that get harder as you go.

list.i1: You fight with a team of up to three cards. Bosses take on your three cards alone.
list.i2: The preparation screen shows the enemies, the rewards, the energy cost and a verdict: Advantage Balanced Risky.
list.i3: Battles play out automatically: speed (SPD) fills each card's action gauge. If time runs out, it's a draw, and the energy is spent anyway.
list.i4: Each card has eight stats: HP, ATK, DEF, SPD, crit rate, crit damage, armor penetration and lifesteal. On top of that come its passive, its element and its equipment.
list.i5: You have a separate team for the campaign, each of the four towers and the raid. Any mode you haven't set up uses your campaign team.

campagne.firstClear: Your first clear of a stage gives guaranteed rewards (gold, dust, XP, sometimes a piece of equipment or a card). Replaying a stage you've already won gives repeatable rewards, with a chance of drops.
campagne.info: On a stage you've already won, Multiple battle chains several fights at once (×1 or ×5) for the matching energy.

elements.intro: Every card and every monster has an element. Attacking with the advantage deals more damage; attacking at a disadvantage deals less.

list.i1: Fire beats Nature, Nature beats Earth, Earth beats Water, Water beats Fire.
list.i2: Light and Dark sit outside the cycle: each one has the advantage over the other.
list.i3: Your cards go for enemies weak to their element first.
list.i4: A chapter's boss has an element that none of the chapter's monsters have: plan a different team for it.

elements.tip: The element guide opens from the campaign and tower headers, and the collection can be filtered by element.

tours.intro: There are four towers, one per element: Ember (fire), Prism (water), Sap (nature) and Monolith (earth). Each has 10 floors that unlock in order.

list.i1: Each tower drops one type of equipment the campaign doesn't: Gloves (Ember), Boots (Prism), Amulet (Sap), Belt (Monolith).
list.i2: Every win gives you a piece; the higher the floor, the better the rarity.
list.i3: Battles cost energy. A floor you've already cleared can be replayed with multiple battle, as in the campaign.
list.i4: A tower's monsters share its element: a team that counters it starts with a big advantage.

combat-points.intro: Energy (combat points) is to battles what tokens are to pulls: it refills on its own up to a cap, shown in the top bar.

list.i1: Every campaign or tower battle costs some. Without energy, the button reads "Not enough energy".
list.i2: Every account level-up refills it to the max.
list.i3: Energy packs from the shop can take it past the cap.
list.i4: Skills in the Combat branch speed up its regeneration, raise the cap and lower the cost of multiple battles.

combat-points.tip: At the cap, regenerated energy is lost: spend it before then.

cartes.intro: To keep up with later stages, your cards need to get stronger. Everything happens on the card's sheet.

i1.title: Level
i1.text: Raise a card's level with gold and dust: its stats go up with every level, up to its tier's cap.

i2.title: Tier & ascension
i2.text: There are 7 tiers of 10 levels. At the top of a tier, ascension uses one duplicate of the card and raises its level cap. Its passive gets stronger up to tier 6; after that, only stats keep growing.

cartes.tip: After a loss: rethink your team's lineup and elements, or level up your cards before going back.

equipement.intro: Every card has 7 slots: Weapon, Armor, Ring, Amulet, Gloves, Boots and Belt. Each piece has a rarity, a main stat and sub-stats.

list.i1: The campaign drops Weapons, Armor and Rings; the towers drop the other four types.
list.i2: You upgrade a piece with gold. At certain levels it gains a sub-stat or improves one.
list.i3: Pieces you don't need can be sold for gold.

equipement.setsIntro: Every piece belongs to a set. Wearing enough pieces of the same set on the same card activates its bonus:
equipement.info: With 7 slots, a card can stack several sets (4 + 3, 3 + 2 + 2…). Sets are counted card by card: two cards wearing two Wrath pieces each activate nothing. The Set bonuses button sums it all up.

quetes.intro: Quests give you goals rewarded with tokens, dust and sometimes XP. They progress on their own as you play.

list.i1: Weekly quests are drawn every Monday (UTC); One-shot quests can only be done once.
list.i2: Collect a finished quest with Claim, on the Quests page.
list.i3: Finishing every weekly quest unlocks the Perfect week bonus, with gold and XP.

succes.intro: Achievements are long-term goals: pulls, rarities obtained, level, login streak, campaign chapters and bosses, flawless wins, sets, recycling…

list.i3: Rewards can include cards, tokens, dust and XP.

chaine.intro: Log in every day to grow your streak. Missing a day resets it; your best streak is kept.

list.i1: Every streak day gives you something, and days 3, 7, 14 and 30 give more (tokens, dust, XP).

recompenses.intro: Level-ups, the login streak, achievements, the raid and events drop rewards to collect in the notification bell.

list.i1: Claim them one by one or all at once. Quest rewards are claimed on the Quests page instead.
list.i2: Some contain a card, revealed when you claim it.

recompenses.info: The badge on the bell shows how many rewards are waiting for you.

i1.title: Collectors
i1.text: Completion rate, distinct cards and variants.

i2.title: Teams
i2.text: The team's combined completion, then variants and number of pulls.

i3.title: Combat
i3.text: Campaign progress; ties are broken by your campaign team's power.

collection.intro: Your collection holds the cards you own, one entry per card and per variant.

list.i1: Filter by rarity, variant, set or element, group by rarity, element or set, and sort by power, level, duplicates or name.
list.i2: You can show every card in the game, including the ones you're missing.
list.i3: A card's sheet lets you level it up, ascend it, manage its equipment, recycle it or add it to your wishlist.
list.i4: Your profile, collection included, is visible to other players.

equipes.intro: A team is a group of players who progress together. Create one or join one from the Teams page; you can be in up to three teams.

list.i1: Three roles: leader, officer and member. The leader can hand the role over.
list.i2: The leader and officers invite by username or email; an invitation expires after 48 hours.
list.i3: A team can open itself to applications: it then shows up in the directory, where any player can apply. The leader and officers accept or decline.

equipes.progression: Team progression: every week, members earn team points (raid damage, pulls, duels and bets won). These points level the team up, and each level gives a point to put into one of four bonuses:

perks.i1: Token flow: faster token regeneration for every member
perks.i2: Raid cadence: extra raid attacks every day

equipes.info: The leader and officers assign the points; only the leader can reset them.

raid.intro: Every week, your team takes on a raid boss whose element changes from week to week. It's in the Raid tab of the team page.

list.i1: Each member has a limited number of attacks per day; the Raid cadence bonus adds more.
list.i2: Every member's damage fills a shared bar.
list.i3: At 25, 50, 75 and 100% of the bar, every participant gets a reward (tokens, gold, dust, and an epic card at 100%), once per week and per team. It lands in the bell.
list.i4: Beating the raid raises next week's difficulty; a week without a win lowers it. Boss HP is calculated as if the team had at least 10 members.

duels.intro: Two ways for teammates to go head to head, from the team page.

i1.title: Pull duel
i1.text: You challenge a teammate: your next pulls count, each on your own side. The higher score wins and takes the cards the other player pulled. The higher the rarity, the more a card is worth, and a brilliant counts one and a half times. On a tie, everyone keeps their cards. While the duel runs, the counted cards can't be recycled.

i2.title: Bets
i2.text: You stake dust on a teammate's next pulls: will they get at least one card of a given rarity? The odds are shown before you confirm, and other teammates can raise on your side or against you, which moves them. The house takes a cut. If the target doesn't pull before the deadline, stakes are refunded.

api.title: Public API & Discord bot
api.intro: Gachapon has a public API, documented in OpenAPI 3.1, to plug a Discord bot or your own tools into your account.

list.i1: Authentication uses the <pill>X-API-Key</pill> header: generate your key in Settings.

cta.title: Your turn.
cta.subtitle: Create your account and pull your first capsule.
